page: Microsoft Azure M624ds_12_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MDSHighMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors providing 624 vCPUs. It features an extensive memory footprint of 11400.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 18.27 GB per vCPU core. Discrete GPU acceleration is not present in this instance.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via a 429 GB solid-state drive, and the virtual machine is capable of attaching Premium Storage volumes. Because the included local disk space is modest relative to the vast memory and compute resources, persistent enterprise storage depends on managed external storage infrastructure.

In qualitative terms, this server profile aggregates compute and memory density into a single host footprint, addressing monolithic architecture needs without the complexity and latency of horizontal cluster distribution. The hardware configuration is aligned with mission-critical enterprise workloads, including massive in-memory databases, large-scale transaction systems, memory-bound simulations, and complex data extraction pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M624ds_12_v3 is a memory-optimized instance within the MDSHighMemoryv3 family, hosted via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with 624 dedicated x86_64 Intel vCPUs paired with 11400.0 GB of system memory, providing a high density of 18.27 GB of RAM per vCPU. It features 429 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage for external disk connectivity, with no GPU acceleration included. The configuration prioritizes vast volatile memory capacity alongside massive parallel processing capability on a single node. Economically, this design maximizes resource density for extreme-scale workloads that cannot easily partition across multiple smaller instances. Microsoft Azure M624ds_12_v3 is primarily engineered for colossal in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning platforms, and intensive in-memory data processing.
